question: Which is the largest container port in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Port**, also widely known as **Nhava Sheva**, is the largest **container port** in India. It is located in **Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra**, along the **Arabian Sea** coast.
 
• It was commissioned on **May 26, 1989**, with the primary objective of de-congesting the **Mumbai Port** and serving as a hub for containerized traffic in the country.
 
• The port handles approximately **50%** of the total containerized cargo across all **major ports** in India. It is currently ranked among the top **30** container ports globally in terms of efficiency and volume.
 
• It serves as the gateway for India's international trade, particularly with **Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas**. The port handles diverse commodities including **textiles, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, carpets, and heavy machinery**.
 
• JNPT is the first major port in India to adopt the **Landlord Port Model**, where the port authority acts as a regulatory body and landlord, while port operations are carried out by **private terminal operators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mundra Port, Gujarat**:
 
 
• Located in the **Kutch district** of **Gujarat**, it is the largest **private port** and the largest **commercial port** in India by overall cargo volume.
 
• It is operated by **Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited (APSEZ)** and has surpassed many major government ports in total tonnage handled annually.
 
 
 
• **Chennai Port, Tamil Nadu**:
 
 
• It is the **second largest** container port in India and the largest port in the **Bay of Bengal** region.
 
• Established in **1881**, it is an **artificial and all-weather port** that plays a crucial role in the handling of **automobiles, iron ore, and agricultural products**.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata Port, West Bengal**:
 
 
• Officially renamed the **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port** in **2020**, it is the only **major riverine port** in India.
 
• Located about **203 kilometers** from the sea on the banks of the **Hooghly River**, it serves as a critical trade link for **North-East India** and landlocked neighbors like **Nepal and Bhutan**.
 
 
 
• **Mumbai Port, Maharashtra**:
 
 
• It is one of the **oldest modern ports** in India, used primarily for **bulk cargo** and **liquid chemicals**. Unlike JNPT, it is a **natural deep-water harbor**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Infrastructure and Connectivity**: **JNPT** is directly connected to the **Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC)**, which significantly reduces the transit time for goods moving between the port and the **National Capital Region (NCR)**.
 
• **TEU Capacity**: The port's performance is measured in **TEUs (Twenty-foot Equivalent Units)**. In the financial year **2022-2023**, JNPT handled a record-breaking **6.05 million TEUs**.
 
• **Special Economic Zone (SEZ)**: A dedicated **Multi-Product SEZ** has been developed at JNPT to promote **manufacturing-led exports** and enhance the "Make in India" initiative.
 
• **Digital Initiatives**: The port has implemented the **Centralized Parking Plaza (CPP)** and **Direct Port Delivery (DPD)** systems to ensure **transparency** and reduce the **Logistics Performance Index (LPI)** costs for traders.
